ce="Zkhr9OLSs8uCY+kA9ikI7zJt" type="application/json" data-nuxt-data="nuxt-app" data-ssr="true" id="__NUXT_DATA__">[["ShallowReactive",1],{"data":2,"state":449,"once":455,"_errors":456,"serverRendered":21,"path":458},["ShallowReactive",3],{"$fcfgpBjXREEgZekZe0J0Dk9Cp9ARoFytgA0SbMSb_KSM":4,"package-data":448,"package-metadata":14},{"description":5,"vulnerabilities":6,"licenses":37,"latestReleaseVersion":45,"latestNonVulnerableVersion":48,"firstPublishedDate":49,"versions":50,"totalVersions":447},"",[7],{"id":8,"title":9,"description":10,"severity":11,"affectedVersions":12,"malicious":17,"cvssScore":24,"publicationTime":25,"identifiers":26,"vulnDescription":33},"SNYK-JAVA-IONETTY-19233598","Null Byte Interaction Error (Poison Null Byte)","## Overview\n\nAffected versions of this package are vulnerable to Null Byte Interaction Error (Poison Null Byte) via the `Socks4ClientEncoder` and `Socks5ClientEncoder` in `codec-socks`. An attacker can truncate or alter encoded SOCKS requests by supplying `userId`, destination host, username, or password values containing embedded NUL bytes. This can make the proxy interpret different credentials or destination names than the application intended, leading to domain spoofing, authentication confusion, and proxy connections being sent to the wrong host.\n## Remediation\nUpgrade `io.netty:netty-codec-socks` to version 4.1.137.Final, 4.2.17.Final or higher.\n## References\n- [GitHub Commit netty-4.1.137.Final](https:\u002F\u002Fgithub.com\u002Fnetty\u002Fnetty\u002Fcommit\u002F9e0519239108a69b7e9bbc5e9182ee139a0d7961)\n- [GitHub Commit netty-4.2.17.Final](https:\u002F\u002Fgithub.com\u002Fnetty\u002Fnetty\u002Fcommit\u002F1b5abc6443b63726c72cdd285af2feb7ddbb8ff7)\n- [Maintainer's Advisory](https:\u002F\u002Fgithub.com\u002Fnetty\u002Fnetty\u002Fsecurity\u002Fadvisories\u002FGHSA-cc6x-ffm5-83wf)\n","medium",[13,18],{"min":14,"max":15},null,{"version":16,"inclusive":17},"4.1.137.Final",false,{"min":19,"max":22},{"version":20,"inclusive":21},"4.2.0.Final",true,{"version":23,"inclusive":17},"4.2.17.Final",6.3,"2026-08-24T05:07:01.479211Z",{"CVE":27,"CWE":29,"GHSA":31},[28],"CVE-2026-62380",[30],"CWE-626",[32],"GHSA-cc6x-ffm5-83wf",{"Overview":34,"Remediation":35,"References":36},"\u003Cp>Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Null Byte Interaction Error (Poison Null Byte) via the \u003Ccode>Socks4ClientEncoder\u003C\u002Fcode> and \u003Ccode>Socks5ClientEncoder\u003C\u002Fcode> in \u003Ccode>codec-socks\u003C\u002Fcode>. An attacker can truncate or alter encoded SOCKS requests by supplying \u003Ccode>userId\u003C\u002Fcode>, destination host, username, or password values containing embedded NUL bytes. This can make the proxy interpret different credentials or destination names than the application intended, leading to domain spoofing, authentication confusion, and proxy connections being sent to
